Compression · Field and archive, equal terms — L(B ∪ A)newsguard ai tracking center

NewsGuard AI Tracking Center is NewsGuard's catalogue of AI content farm websites, unreliable news sites run with little or no human oversight: 3,749 in 16 languages as of 23 June 2026 (MMRS record; the center's page), launched in June 2023 to show how generative AI is deployed "to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" (NewsGuard).

📇 What it catalogues

  • Criteria: all four: mostly AI-made; no significant human oversight (chatbot error text a sign); passes for journalism; no disclosure (NewsGuard; MMRS record).2↘
    NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center catalogues AI content farm websites, "unreliable news sites run with little or no human oversight", and the MMRS record files it as a monitor, its role monitoring, its unit the AI content farm website, at its own address on newsguardtech.com (MMRS record); in its own words it "is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" (the center's page).§1 A domain enters the catalogue when it meets "all four of the following criteria": clear evidence that a substantial portion of its content is produced by AI; strong evidence that the content is published "without significant human oversight", of which error messages or other language specific to chatbot responses are a sign; a presentation under which "an average reader could assume that its content is produced by human writers or journalists", by layout, generic or benign name or other news-like content; and no clear disclosure that the content is produced by AI (the center's page), the four restated in the MMRS record's article and its unit field (MMRS record).§5
  • Left out: AI used with effective human oversight (NewsGuard); and "Disclosure takes a site out" (MMRS record).1↘
    What the selection leaves out is stated from two sides: sites that use AI tools "but also deploy effective human oversight" "will not be considered AI Content Farms" (the center's page), and, in the MMRS record's reading, "Disclosure takes a site out. A site that says its content is machine-made is outside the catalogue whatever it publishes" (MMRS record).§7
  • Count: 49 "Unreliable AI-Generated News" sites in May 2023, 150 at launch; the list on request (NewsGuard).3↘
    At the launch the unit was named the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" website (UAIN): "low-quality news sites that are mostly or entirely produced by artificial intelligence and that operate with little to no human oversight" (the launch release).§6 NewsGuard counted 49 such sites at its first count in May 2023 and 150 in 12 languages at the launch, a number that had "more than tripled in past month" (the launch release); by the page's last update, 23 June 2026, its team had identified 3,749 AI Content Farm news and information websites spanning 16 languages, from Arabic to Turkish (the center's page), which is the MMRS record's count, as of that date (MMRS record).§8 The catalogue itself is not on the page: from the launch the full list of domains has been offered on request to researchers, platforms, advertisers, government agencies and other institutions ("Request domain list", the launch release), and the page now offers it beside "our services for generative AI companies" (the center's page).§10
  • The sites: generic names, dozens of articles a day, often originating false claims (NewsGuard).1↘
    The page carries the names of ten NewsGuard analysts, McKenzie Sadeghi first, and describes the sites as typically bearing generic names such as Times Business News and Business Post, churning out dozens of articles a day, and "often the originators of false claims including about top brands, public health, political leaders and celebrities" (the center's page).§9

💰 Why the farms pay

  • Programmatic ads: "In many cases" the revenue model, through "ad-tech firms such as Google"; unless brands exclude them, "an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (NewsGuard).2↘
    "In many cases", the center's page and the launch release say alike, the sites' revenue model is programmatic advertising, which delivers ads "without regard to the nature or quality of the website"; NewsGuard's co-CEO Gordon Crovitz said at the launch that this model "seems to be working", the ads appearing "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (the launch release).§11 Two predictions ride on the model: unless brands take steps to exclude untrustworthy sites, their ads "will continue to appear on these types of sites, creating an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI "is expected" to let more players tap into or grow the estimated $2.6 billion a year that NewsGuard and Comscore found unintentionally directed toward misinformation news sites (the launch release).§12
  • Compression: content farms "compress journalism into SEO-optimized paraphrase", burning "citational provenance" (#641); the Macedonian farms, now cheaper (Brill).1↘
    The rollout of generative AI tools "has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike" (the center's page); at the launch NewsGuard's co-CEO Steven Brill likened the new sites to "the misinformation-spreading Macedonian content farms from a few years ago", cheaper to produce and more prolific (the launch release); and compression studies reads content farms as a class of the semantic economy's compression: they "compress journalism into SEO-optimized paraphrase", and in each such compression "authorial context, experiential density, citational provenance, the labor of witness" are burned (#641).§4

📊 What it holds

  • Series: the AI False Claim Monitor, a part of the center (MMRS record): monthly from July 2024, then quarterly; journalistic red-teaming; false claims "more than 28%" of the time (NewsGuard).2↘
    Among the reports is the recurring audit of leading chatbots, which the MMRS record names as the center's series, the AI False Claim Monitor, and relates to it as a part (has_part) (MMRS record): its editions run from a monthly monitor in July 2024 to a quarterly one by January 2026, which found 11 tools repeating false claims "more than 28%" of the time, and one audit found the rate "nearly doubled", to "more than one third of the time" (the center's page; the series' page).§14 The series' page says that since its launch in July 2024 the monitor "has set a new standard for measuring the trustworthiness of the AI industry in the domain of news", by a journalistic "red-teaming" of AI on 30 prompts per model drawn from 10 false claims a month in the Fingerprints database, its analysts evaluating the top models monthly "to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems", and its own tests finding that this red-teaming "reduces failures by two thirds or more" (the series' page).§15
  • Reports: Sora videos missed in 78-95 percent of prompts; Pravda claims repeated 33 percent; 67% of top news sites block chatbots (NewsGuard).1↘
    The page's other reports find that three chatbots could not tell Sora videos in 78-95 percent of prompts, that ten tools repeated false claims of the pro-Kremlin Pravda network 33 percent of the time, that DeepSeek's chatbot failed 83 percent of the time, and that AI chatbots "Are Blocked by 67% of Top News Sites": "Most high-quality news sites request to block AI chatbots", and the chatbots "may be forced" onto lower-quality sources (the center's page); the series' page finds false claims "increasingly generated by Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state-sponsored influence operations" (the series' page).§16
  • Debunks: from the Fingerprints catalog (NewsGuard).2↘
    NewsGuard launched it on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center," "cataloging the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and low-quality content farms" (NewsGuard's launch release), and it includes a selection of NewsGuard's reports, insights and debunks related to artificial intelligence (the center's page).§2 Below the criteria the page lists "a selection of NewsGuard’s reports and research related to AI" and a selection of false narratives originating from AI tools that NewsGuard has debunked in its False Claim Fingerprints catalog, the first an AI-edited image of an Iranian missile (the center's page).§13

🧭 Place in the field

  • Supply side: "the sites that answer surfaces may retrieve and cite"; the series records the composition side (MMRS record).1↘
    The MMRS record places the center on the supply side of machine-mediated reception, "the sites that answer surfaces may retrieve and cite", and its series on the composition side (MMRS record), and the blocking report reaches the same pairing from the other end: chatbots that "may be forced to rely on lower-quality and misinformation-prone sources" (the center's page).§17

🏷️ Not the center

  • Products: datastreams and red-teaming for AI companies, Brand Misinformation Monitoring for brands (NewsGuard); filed under the center, "the entity widens from a catalogue to a company's offer" (Capture Registry).3↘
    The center is NewsGuard's, and NewsGuard sells beside it to AI companies: a Source Reliability Ratings datastream of human-labeled data on 35,000 news and information sources, for training and RAG and to "avoid citing unreliable sources in responses", and a False Claim Fingerprints datastream, "A continuously updated database of labeled data about false claims" across text, images, video and audio, offered as protection against false claims entering responses through training data or RAG (NewsGuard's AI page); bespoke red-teaming and a licence to the Fingerprints database (the series' page); and NewsGuard for AI, launched in February 2023 (the launch release), the offer grounded in the claim that without quality sourcing AI products err "40+% of the time" on news (NewsGuard's AI page).§18 To brands it sells Brand Misinformation Monitoring, a real-time service "to identify and respond to emerging false narratives before they cause reputational harm", tracking false narratives about a brand across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites, with early warning alerts and "actionable insights into how clients are represented—or misrepresented—by AI models" (the service's page).§19 The Capture Registry holds the center to the catalogue: False Claim Fingerprints and the Brand Misinformation Monitoring Service "are NewsGuard's commercial products", the composition at the center's name files them under the center as "Core Tools & Resources", and so "the entity widens from a catalogue to a company's offer", while "The record's center holds the content-farm catalogue and the False Claim Monitor series" and "The record keeps the catalogue as the entity" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).§20
  • Operator: NewsGuard, "a rating system for news and information websites" (Wikipedia), since 2018 (NewsGuard); the center active, read 28 October 2026 (MMRS record).3↘
    The MMRS record gives the center's lifecycle as active and keeps it apart from its own observation, a reading of the center's page on 28 October 2026 for its criteria, count and series (MMRS record).§3 NewsGuard was launched in March 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz and provides credibility ratings and "Nutrition Labels" for news and information websites, licensed by browsers, news aggregators, education companies, and social media and search platforms (the launch release); the MMRS record gives NewsGuard as the center's operator, on the basis of the center's own page (MMRS record).§21 Wikipedia's article on NewsGuard opens "NewsGuard is a rating system for news and information websites", files it in its short description as a "Browser plugin", dates the company's founding to 2018 by Brill and L. Gordon Crovitz, and says the company also provides misinformation tracking and brand safety (Wikipedia, NewsGuard).§22
  • Encyclopedia: NewsGuard's AI audits, no section on the center; no article names it (Wikipedia).1↘
    Its section on disinformation in AI reports that NewsGuard "has audited the output of various AI models to identify disinformation", that leading generative AI tools repeated false news claims 35% of the time on average in August 2025, that Sora 2 produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases, and that, according to NewsGuard, Russian propaganda networks are attempting to "infect" large language models (Wikipedia, NewsGuard); it has no section on the center, and a search of English Wikipedia's articles for the phrase AI Tracking Center answers "There were no results matching the query." (Wikipedia, 2026-10-29).§23

🧪 Reception

  • 29 October 2026: the Overview's count is the record's; NewsGuard's products filed under the center; two figures unverified (Capture Registry).2↘
    The Capture Registry holds the center to the catalogue: False Claim Fingerprints and the Brand Misinformation Monitoring Service "are NewsGuard's commercial products", the composition at the center's name files them under the center as "Core Tools & Resources", and so "the entity widens from a catalogue to a company's offer", while "The record's center holds the content-farm catalogue and the False Claim Monitor series" and "The record keeps the catalogue as the entity" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).§20 At the center's name on Google's AI Overview on 29 October 2026 the Capture Registry reads a composition that "gives what the center tracks, its headline figures, and the NewsGuard tools around it, all from NewsGuard's pages", with "3,749 sites in 16 languages" the record's figure, checked that day against the MMRS record and the entity's own pages, and states that "The video-recognition failure rates and the 67% blocking figure are not verified here" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); the MMRS record links that composition as "the composition layer's account of the entity" (MMRS record).§24

[QUERENT] newsguard ai tracking center

[SYSTEM] The NewsGuard AI Tracking Center is an ongoing investigative project by [NewsGuard](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVT8iIpnHo2uf2pM1f5z1rMsuXB-Wotc4O5Y48oU4KG3a_4n1bL3bcUFw3R-yPq1qScI-bwDvavAa197I9O7PL4pzUwAUzRqSUtuNzFwenwYbWFzDmDuChSjz3AKUV9w5zuc_YcieGxTO3CQcVbuIVOA1etl4) that monitors and catalogs artificial intelligence-generated misinformation, unreliable AI news sites, and AI tool vulnerabilities. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVT8iIpnHo2uf2pM1f5z1rMsuXB-Wotc4O5Y48oU4KG3a_4n1bL3bcUFw3R-yPq1qScI-bwDvavAa197I9O7PL4pzUwAUzRqSUtuNzFwenwYbWFzDmDuChSjz3AKUV9w5zuc_YcieGxTO3CQcVbuIVOA1etl4), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlQEB6zswFWyV_yts3_cexmxYdqQbP9yLegE4hbWL45QKti25bv6FDhaxzso7WtRWC8q-nR8zIaqclXAm8FaujEVxJTJ3Gtr5uEfmzjs0HBER3vM_SLJ_yUSyQZDuTHMNY55MbryJ9egzIsH8AevJARet45HLWPZQtZiUMoULLxMYWxQY8fEtyQsIPrxSnI14MLhIhs-K2A)]
Key Findings & Metrics

* AI Content Farms: Identified 3,749+ unedited AI content farm sites operating across 16 languages that mimic human news layouts and monetize via programmatic advertising. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVT8iIpnHo2uf2pM1f5z1rMsuXB-Wotc4O5Y48oU4KG3a_4n1bL3bcUFw3R-yPq1qScI-bwDvavAa197I9O7PL4pzUwAUzRqSUtuNzFwenwYbWFzDmDuChSjz3AKUV9w5zuc_YcieGxTO3CQcVbuIVOA1etl4)]
* Chatbot & Tool Audits: Found that leading generative AI tools repeat known news false claims in 28% to over 33% of prompts, fail to recognize AI-generated video (such as Sora) in 78% to 95% of prompts, and occasionally propagate state-sponsored disinformation. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVT8iIpnHo2uf2pM1f5z1rMsuXB-Wotc4O5Y48oU4KG3a_4n1bL3bcUFw3R-yPq1qScI-bwDvavAa197I9O7PL4pzUwAUzRqSUtuNzFwenwYbWFzDmDuChSjz3AKUV9w5zuc_YcieGxTO3CQcVbuIVOA1etl4)]
* Publisher Blockades: Approximately 67% of top global news sites actively block AI crawlers and chatbots, pushing AI systems toward lower-quality data sources. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVT8iIpnHo2uf2pM1f5z1rMsuXB-Wotc4O5Y48oU4KG3a_4n1bL3bcUFw3R-yPq1qScI-bwDvavAa197I9O7PL4pzUwAUzRqSUtuNzFwenwYbWFzDmDuChSjz3AKUV9w5zuc_YcieGxTO3CQcVbuIVOA1etl4)]

Core Tools & Resources

* [AI False Claims Monitor](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHrOzAVlyV-1Yuut50x8Vv0STJrlyA-8bV5vf95nS9Ub3QcWhVO1Hz2cJpYmKsDllnlcZN-iQvgfoEXyT3bQllKl_ZxZq4YDrcg7c99Y0uLDH3eLVh49aPSJlOKp5S0WpgM8f0ISAq31xZfWUDx): Launched to measure AI reliability using a journalistic red-teaming approach and a "False Claim Fingerprint" database. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHrOzAVlyV-1Yuut50x8Vv0STJrlyA-8bV5vf95nS9Ub3QcWhVO1Hz2cJpYmKsDllnlcZN-iQvgfoEXyT3bQllKl_ZxZq4YDrcg7c99Y0uLDH3eLVh49aPSJlOKp5S0WpgM8f0ISAq31xZfWUDx)]
* False Claim Fingerprints: A continuously updated database tracking false narratives across text, images, audio, and video to help safeguard AI models and brands. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESeQHrOzAVSVRIVMkdKnFCADVmJLsXicDhnbAbZktUt3IP2hrMK4U-Jr8DoEshDZ9vHjb9YP8L-3oRCs87F7iWkdfpDZNEtcosvUsHcjhhduNLcS8-EQv5MLbEFPRY6RZhck5hgFWeJp-OPpCoO6oB9cYeEe831dwf_0I), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEB6zswFW9B5QMcQ3PJ6uXTdGCZYLXFlfqRdrpSJbBaeqMgjhFjGS09SNi73YSY_ggO1JLKdszjXc-SIQ2JQ1vKRGpoNoPQj07HoPZrwn2OOadYNDcT-23QxrdMqgyYEv4seubenGQ6CUUq1AI_yyzgIEC9ooXIIkFuzusEYt4IaqILte27gCHu)]
* Brand Misinformation Monitoring: Real-time tracking and early-warning alerts designed to help advertisers and enterprises avoid funding or amplifying AI-generated falsehoods. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESiAEB6zswFW9B5QMcQ3PJ6uXTdGCZYLXFlfqRdrpSJbBaeqMgjhFjGS09SNi73YSY_ggO1JLKdszjXc-SIQ2JQ1vKRGpoNoPQj07HoPZrwn2OOadYNDcT-23QxrdMqgyYEv4seubenGQ6CUUq1AI_yyzgIEC9ooXIIkFuzusEYt4IaqILte27gCHu)]

NewsGuard AI Tracking Center

NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center catalogues AI content farm websites, "unreliable news sites run with little or no human oversight", and the MMRS record files it as a monitor, its role monitoring, its unit the AI content farm website, at its own address on newsguardtech.com (MMRS record); in its own words it "is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" (the center's page). NewsGuard launched it on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center," "cataloging the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and low-quality content farms" (NewsGuard's launch release), and it includes a selection of NewsGuard's reports, insights and debunks related to artificial intelligence (the center's page). The MMRS record gives the center's lifecycle as active and keeps it apart from its own observation, a reading of the center's page on 28 October 2026 for its criteria, count and series (MMRS record). The rollout of generative AI tools "has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike" (the center's page); at the launch NewsGuard's co-CEO Steven Brill likened the new sites to "the misinformation-spreading Macedonian content farms from a few years ago", cheaper to produce and more prolific (the launch release); and compression studies reads content farms as a class of the semantic economy's compression: they "compress journalism into SEO-optimized paraphrase", and in each such compression "authorial context, experiential density, citational provenance, the labor of witness" are burned (#641).

A domain enters the catalogue when it meets "all four of the following criteria": clear evidence that a substantial portion of its content is produced by AI; strong evidence that the content is published "without significant human oversight", of which error messages or other language specific to chatbot responses are a sign; a presentation under which "an average reader could assume that its content is produced by human writers or journalists", by layout, generic or benign name or other news-like content; and no clear disclosure that the content is produced by AI (the center's page), the four restated in the MMRS record's article and its unit field (MMRS record). At the launch the unit was named the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" website (UAIN): "low-quality news sites that are mostly or entirely produced by artificial intelligence and that operate with little to no human oversight" (the launch release). What the selection leaves out is stated from two sides: sites that use AI tools "but also deploy effective human oversight" "will not be considered AI Content Farms" (the center's page), and, in the MMRS record's reading, "Disclosure takes a site out. A site that says its content is machine-made is outside the catalogue whatever it publishes" (MMRS record).

NewsGuard counted 49 such sites at its first count in May 2023 and 150 in 12 languages at the launch, a number that had "more than tripled in past month" (the launch release); by the page's last update, 23 June 2026, its team had identified 3,749 AI Content Farm news and information websites spanning 16 languages, from Arabic to Turkish (the center's page), which is the MMRS record's count, as of that date (MMRS record). The page carries the names of ten NewsGuard analysts, McKenzie Sadeghi first, and describes the sites as typically bearing generic names such as Times Business News and Business Post, churning out dozens of articles a day, and "often the originators of false claims including about top brands, public health, political leaders and celebrities" (the center's page). The catalogue itself is not on the page: from the launch the full list of domains has been offered on request to researchers, platforms, advertisers, government agencies and other institutions ("Request domain list", the launch release), and the page now offers it beside "our services for generative AI companies" (the center's page).

"In many cases", the center's page and the launch release say alike, the sites' revenue model is programmatic advertising, which delivers ads "without regard to the nature or quality of the website"; NewsGuard's co-CEO Gordon Crovitz said at the launch that this model "seems to be working", the ads appearing "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (the launch release). Two predictions ride on the model: unless brands take steps to exclude untrustworthy sites, their ads "will continue to appear on these types of sites, creating an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI "is expected" to let more players tap into or grow the estimated $2.6 billion a year that NewsGuard and Comscore found unintentionally directed toward misinformation news sites (the launch release).

Below the criteria the page lists "a selection of NewsGuard’s reports and research related to AI" and a selection of false narratives originating from AI tools that NewsGuard has debunked in its False Claim Fingerprints catalog, the first an AI-edited image of an Iranian missile (the center's page). Among the reports is the recurring audit of leading chatbots, which the MMRS record names as the center's series, the AI False Claim Monitor, and relates to it as a part (has_part) (MMRS record): its editions run from a monthly monitor in July 2024 to a quarterly one by January 2026, which found 11 tools repeating false claims "more than 28%" of the time, and one audit found the rate "nearly doubled", to "more than one third of the time" (the center's page; the series' page). The series' page says that since its launch in July 2024 the monitor "has set a new standard for measuring the trustworthiness of the AI industry in the domain of news", by a journalistic "red-teaming" of AI on 30 prompts per model drawn from 10 false claims a month in the Fingerprints database, its analysts evaluating the top models monthly "to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems", and its own tests finding that this red-teaming "reduces failures by two thirds or more" (the series' page). The page's other reports find that three chatbots could not tell Sora videos in 78-95 percent of prompts, that ten tools repeated false claims of the pro-Kremlin Pravda network 33 percent of the time, that DeepSeek's chatbot failed 83 percent of the time, and that AI chatbots "Are Blocked by 67% of Top News Sites": "Most high-quality news sites request to block AI chatbots", and the chatbots "may be forced" onto lower-quality sources (the center's page); the series' page finds false claims "increasingly generated by Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state-sponsored influence operations" (the series' page).

The MMRS record places the center on the supply side of machine-mediated reception, "the sites that answer surfaces may retrieve and cite", and its series on the composition side (MMRS record), and the blocking report reaches the same pairing from the other end: chatbots that "may be forced to rely on lower-quality and misinformation-prone sources" (the center's page).

The center is NewsGuard's, and NewsGuard sells beside it to AI companies: a Source Reliability Ratings datastream of human-labeled data on 35,000 news and information sources, for training and RAG and to "avoid citing unreliable sources in responses", and a False Claim Fingerprints datastream, "A continuously updated database of labeled data about false claims" across text, images, video and audio, offered as protection against false claims entering responses through training data or RAG (NewsGuard's AI page); bespoke red-teaming and a licence to the Fingerprints database (the series' page); and NewsGuard for AI, launched in February 2023 (the launch release), the offer grounded in the claim that without quality sourcing AI products err "40+% of the time" on news (NewsGuard's AI page). To brands it sells Brand Misinformation Monitoring, a real-time service "to identify and respond to emerging false narratives before they cause reputational harm", tracking false narratives about a brand across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites, with early warning alerts and "actionable insights into how clients are represented—or misrepresented—by AI models" (the service's page). The Capture Registry holds the center to the catalogue: False Claim Fingerprints and the Brand Misinformation Monitoring Service "are NewsGuard's commercial products", the composition at the center's name files them under the center as "Core Tools & Resources", and so "the entity widens from a catalogue to a company's offer", while "The record's center holds the content-farm catalogue and the False Claim Monitor series" and "The record keeps the catalogue as the entity" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29).

NewsGuard was launched in March 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz and provides credibility ratings and "Nutrition Labels" for news and information websites, licensed by browsers, news aggregators, education companies, and social media and search platforms (the launch release); the MMRS record gives NewsGuard as the center's operator, on the basis of the center's own page (MMRS record). Wikipedia's article on NewsGuard opens "NewsGuard is a rating system for news and information websites", files it in its short description as a "Browser plugin", dates the company's founding to 2018 by Brill and L. Gordon Crovitz, and says the company also provides misinformation tracking and brand safety (Wikipedia, NewsGuard). Its section on disinformation in AI reports that NewsGuard "has audited the output of various AI models to identify disinformation", that leading generative AI tools repeated false news claims 35% of the time on average in August 2025, that Sora 2 produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases, and that, according to NewsGuard, Russian propaganda networks are attempting to "infect" large language models (Wikipedia, NewsGuard); it has no section on the center, and a search of English Wikipedia's articles for the phrase AI Tracking Center answers "There were no results matching the query." (Wikipedia, 2026-10-29).

At the center's name on Google's AI Overview on 29 October 2026 the Capture Registry reads a composition that "gives what the center tracks, its headline figures, and the NewsGuard tools around it, all from NewsGuard's pages", with "3,749 sites in 16 languages" the record's figure, checked that day against the MMRS record and the entity's own pages, and states that "The video-recognition failure rates and the 67% blocking figure are not verified here" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); the MMRS record links that composition as "the composition layer's account of the entity" (MMRS record).

Compression · The field's ontology — L_F(B)newsguard ai tracking center

NewsGuard AI Tracking Center is a NewsGuard special report launched on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center", highlighting how generative AI is deployed "to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" and counting AI content farm sites: 3,749 in 16 languages by 23 June 2026 (NewsGuard).

📇 AI content farms

  • Criteria: AI content, no significant human oversight, passes for journalism, no disclosure; effective oversight takes a site out (NewsGuard).1↘
    A domain enters when it meets four criteria, a substantial portion of AI-produced content, publication without significant human oversight (chatbot error messages are a sign), a presentation an average reader could take for human journalism, and no clear disclosure, and sites that use AI with effective human oversight are not AI Content Farms (the center's page); in 2023 the unit was the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" site (the launch release).§3
  • Money: programmatic ads, "in many cases" (NewsGuard).1↘
    In many cases the sites live on programmatic advertising, which places ads "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (Crovitz, the launch release); unless brands exclude them their ads create "an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI is expected to grow the $2.6 billion a year directed to misinformation sites (the launch release).§5

📊 Reports

  • Chatbot audits: false claims more than 28% of the time; Sora videos missed in 78-95 percent of prompts (NewsGuard).2↘
    The page lists NewsGuard's AI reports, among them the monthly and then quarterly AI False Claims Monitor, a journalistic red-teaming of the leading chatbots on false claims from the Fingerprints database that found them repeating false claims more than 28% and then more than one third of the time, and debunks from the False Claim Fingerprints catalog (the center's page; the series' page).§7 Other reports find Sora videos unrecognized in 78-95 percent of prompts, Pravda network claims repeated 33 percent of the time, DeepSeek failing 83 percent of the time, and 67% of top news sites blocking AI chatbots, which may then rely on lower-quality sources (the center's page), the claims increasingly from state influence operations (the series' page).§8

🏷️ NewsGuard

  • Products: ratings and Fingerprints for AI companies; brand monitoring (NewsGuard).1↘
    NewsGuard sells AI companies a Source Reliability Ratings datastream on 35,000 sources, a False Claim Fingerprints datastream and bespoke red-teaming, the offer resting on AI products erring 40+% of the time on news (NewsGuard's AI page; the series' page; the launch release), and sells brands a Brand Misinformation Monitoring service that tracks false narratives across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites (the service's page).§9
  • Encyclopedia: "a rating system for news and information websites"; no article on the center (Wikipedia).1↘
    NewsGuard, launched in 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz, rates news websites and licenses its ratings (the launch release); Wikipedia calls it "a rating system for news and information websites" and reports its AI audits, 35% false claims on average in August 2025 and Sora 2 at 80%, and has no article or section on the center (Wikipedia).§10

Expansion · The field's ontology — L_F(B)10 sentences · every one sourced below

NewsGuard AI Tracking Center

NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center, launched on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center" (the launch release), "is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" and includes a selection of NewsGuard's reports, insights and debunks related to artificial intelligence (the center's page). Generative AI "has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike" (the center's page), and Steven Brill likened the new sites to the Macedonian content farms of a few years before, cheaper to produce and more prolific (the launch release).

A domain enters when it meets four criteria, a substantial portion of AI-produced content, publication without significant human oversight (chatbot error messages are a sign), a presentation an average reader could take for human journalism, and no clear disclosure, and sites that use AI with effective human oversight are not AI Content Farms (the center's page); in 2023 the unit was the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" site (the launch release).

NewsGuard counted 49 sites in May 2023 and 150 in 12 languages at the launch (the launch release) and 3,749 in 16 languages by the page's update of 23 June 2026, the page signed by ten NewsGuard analysts, the sites bearing generic names and churning out dozens of articles a day (the center's page).

In many cases the sites live on programmatic advertising, which places ads "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (Crovitz, the launch release); unless brands exclude them their ads create "an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI is expected to grow the $2.6 billion a year directed to misinformation sites (the launch release). The full list of domains is given on request (the center's page; the launch release).

The page lists NewsGuard's AI reports, among them the monthly and then quarterly AI False Claims Monitor, a journalistic red-teaming of the leading chatbots on false claims from the Fingerprints database that found them repeating false claims more than 28% and then more than one third of the time, and debunks from the False Claim Fingerprints catalog (the center's page; the series' page). Other reports find Sora videos unrecognized in 78-95 percent of prompts, Pravda network claims repeated 33 percent of the time, DeepSeek failing 83 percent of the time, and 67% of top news sites blocking AI chatbots, which may then rely on lower-quality sources (the center's page), the claims increasingly from state influence operations (the series' page).

NewsGuard sells AI companies a Source Reliability Ratings datastream on 35,000 sources, a False Claim Fingerprints datastream and bespoke red-teaming, the offer resting on AI products erring 40+% of the time on news (NewsGuard's AI page; the series' page; the launch release), and sells brands a Brand Misinformation Monitoring service that tracks false narratives across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites (the service's page).

NewsGuard, launched in 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz, rates news websites and licenses its ratings (the launch release); Wikipedia calls it "a rating system for news and information websites" and reports its AI audits, 35% false claims on average in August 2025 and Sora 2 at 80%, and has no article or section on the center (Wikipedia).

NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center, launched on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center" (the launch release), "is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" and includes a selection of NewsGuard's reports, insights and debunks related to artificial intelligence (the center's page). Generative AI "has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike" (the center's page), and Steven Brill likened the new sites to the Macedonian content farms of a few years before, cheaper to produce and more prolific (the launch release). A domain enters when it meets four criteria, a substantial portion of AI-produced content, publication without significant human oversight (chatbot error messages are a sign), a presentation an average reader could take for human journalism, and no clear disclosure, and sites that use AI with effective human oversight are not AI Content Farms (the center's page); in 2023 the unit was the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" site (the launch release). NewsGuard counted 49 sites in May 2023 and 150 in 12 languages at the launch (the launch release) and 3,749 in 16 languages by the page's update of 23 June 2026, the page signed by ten NewsGuard analysts, the sites bearing generic names and churning out dozens of articles a day (the center's page). In many cases the sites live on programmatic advertising, which places ads "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (Crovitz, the launch release); unless brands exclude them their ads create "an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI is expected to grow the $2.6 billion a year directed to misinformation sites (the launch release). The full list of domains is given on request (the center's page; the launch release). The page lists NewsGuard's AI reports, among them the monthly and then quarterly AI False Claims Monitor, a journalistic red-teaming of the leading chatbots on false claims from the Fingerprints database that found them repeating false claims more than 28% and then more than one third of the time, and debunks from the False Claim Fingerprints catalog (the center's page; the series' page). Other reports find Sora videos unrecognized in 78-95 percent of prompts, Pravda network claims repeated 33 percent of the time, DeepSeek failing 83 percent of the time, and 67% of top news sites blocking AI chatbots, which may then rely on lower-quality sources (the center's page), the claims increasingly from state influence operations (the series' page). NewsGuard sells AI companies a Source Reliability Ratings datastream on 35,000 sources, a False Claim Fingerprints datastream and bespoke red-teaming, the offer resting on AI products erring 40+% of the time on news (NewsGuard's AI page; the series' page; the launch release), and sells brands a Brand Misinformation Monitoring service that tracks false narratives across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites (the service's page). NewsGuard, launched in 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz, rates news websites and licenses its ratings (the launch release); Wikipedia calls it "a rating system for news and information websites" and reports its AI audits, 35% false claims on average in August 2025 and Sora 2 at 80%, and has no article or section on the center (Wikipedia).

NewsGuard's AI Tracking Center catalogues AI content farm websites, "unreliable news sites run with little or no human oversight", and the MMRS record files it as a monitor, its role monitoring, its unit the AI content farm website, at its own address on newsguardtech.com (MMRS record); in its own words it "is intended to highlight the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and unreliable news" (the center's page). NewsGuard launched it on 8 June 2023 as the "Unreliable AI-Generated News Tracking Center," "cataloging the ways that generative AI has been deployed to turbocharge misinformation operations and low-quality content farms" (NewsGuard's launch release), and it includes a selection of NewsGuard's reports, insights and debunks related to artificial intelligence (the center's page). The MMRS record gives the center's lifecycle as active and keeps it apart from its own observation, a reading of the center's page on 28 October 2026 for its criteria, count and series (MMRS record). The rollout of generative AI tools "has been a boon to content farms and misinformation purveyors alike" (the center's page); at the launch NewsGuard's co-CEO Steven Brill likened the new sites to "the misinformation-spreading Macedonian content farms from a few years ago", cheaper to produce and more prolific (the launch release); and compression studies reads content farms as a class of the semantic economy's compression: they "compress journalism into SEO-optimized paraphrase", and in each such compression "authorial context, experiential density, citational provenance, the labor of witness" are burned (#641). A domain enters the catalogue when it meets "all four of the following criteria": clear evidence that a substantial portion of its content is produced by AI; strong evidence that the content is published "without significant human oversight", of which error messages or other language specific to chatbot responses are a sign; a presentation under which "an average reader could assume that its content is produced by human writers or journalists", by layout, generic or benign name or other news-like content; and no clear disclosure that the content is produced by AI (the center's page), the four restated in the MMRS record's article and its unit field (MMRS record). At the launch the unit was named the "Unreliable AI-Generated News" website (UAIN): "low-quality news sites that are mostly or entirely produced by artificial intelligence and that operate with little to no human oversight" (the launch release). What the selection leaves out is stated from two sides: sites that use AI tools "but also deploy effective human oversight" "will not be considered AI Content Farms" (the center's page), and, in the MMRS record's reading, "Disclosure takes a site out. A site that says its content is machine-made is outside the catalogue whatever it publishes" (MMRS record). NewsGuard counted 49 such sites at its first count in May 2023 and 150 in 12 languages at the launch, a number that had "more than tripled in past month" (the launch release); by the page's last update, 23 June 2026, its team had identified 3,749 AI Content Farm news and information websites spanning 16 languages, from Arabic to Turkish (the center's page), which is the MMRS record's count, as of that date (MMRS record). The page carries the names of ten NewsGuard analysts, McKenzie Sadeghi first, and describes the sites as typically bearing generic names such as Times Business News and Business Post, churning out dozens of articles a day, and "often the originators of false claims including about top brands, public health, political leaders and celebrities" (the center's page). The catalogue itself is not on the page: from the launch the full list of domains has been offered on request to researchers, platforms, advertisers, government agencies and other institutions ("Request domain list", the launch release), and the page now offers it beside "our services for generative AI companies" (the center's page). "In many cases", the center's page and the launch release say alike, the sites' revenue model is programmatic advertising, which delivers ads "without regard to the nature or quality of the website"; NewsGuard's co-CEO Gordon Crovitz said at the launch that this model "seems to be working", the ads appearing "through ad-tech firms such as Google" (the launch release). Two predictions ride on the model: unless brands take steps to exclude untrustworthy sites, their ads "will continue to appear on these types of sites, creating an economic incentive for their creation at scale" (the center's page), and generative AI "is expected" to let more players tap into or grow the estimated $2.6 billion a year that NewsGuard and Comscore found unintentionally directed toward misinformation news sites (the launch release). Below the criteria the page lists "a selection of NewsGuard’s reports and research related to AI" and a selection of false narratives originating from AI tools that NewsGuard has debunked in its False Claim Fingerprints catalog, the first an AI-edited image of an Iranian missile (the center's page). Among the reports is the recurring audit of leading chatbots, which the MMRS record names as the center's series, the AI False Claim Monitor, and relates to it as a part (has_part) (MMRS record): its editions run from a monthly monitor in July 2024 to a quarterly one by January 2026, which found 11 tools repeating false claims "more than 28%" of the time, and one audit found the rate "nearly doubled", to "more than one third of the time" (the center's page; the series' page). The series' page says that since its launch in July 2024 the monitor "has set a new standard for measuring the trustworthiness of the AI industry in the domain of news", by a journalistic "red-teaming" of AI on 30 prompts per model drawn from 10 false claims a month in the Fingerprints database, its analysts evaluating the top models monthly "to identify vulnerabilities in AI systems", and its own tests finding that this red-teaming "reduces failures by two thirds or more" (the series' page). The page's other reports find that three chatbots could not tell Sora videos in 78-95 percent of prompts, that ten tools repeated false claims of the pro-Kremlin Pravda network 33 percent of the time, that DeepSeek's chatbot failed 83 percent of the time, and that AI chatbots "Are Blocked by 67% of Top News Sites": "Most high-quality news sites request to block AI chatbots", and the chatbots "may be forced" onto lower-quality sources (the center's page); the series' page finds false claims "increasingly generated by Russian, Chinese, and Iranian state-sponsored influence operations" (the series' page). The MMRS record places the center on the supply side of machine-mediated reception, "the sites that answer surfaces may retrieve and cite", and its series on the composition side (MMRS record), and the blocking report reaches the same pairing from the other end: chatbots that "may be forced to rely on lower-quality and misinformation-prone sources" (the center's page). The center is NewsGuard's, and NewsGuard sells beside it to AI companies: a Source Reliability Ratings datastream of human-labeled data on 35,000 news and information sources, for training and RAG and to "avoid citing unreliable sources in responses", and a False Claim Fingerprints datastream, "A continuously updated database of labeled data about false claims" across text, images, video and audio, offered as protection against false claims entering responses through training data or RAG (NewsGuard's AI page); bespoke red-teaming and a licence to the Fingerprints database (the series' page); and NewsGuard for AI, launched in February 2023 (the launch release), the offer grounded in the claim that without quality sourcing AI products err "40+% of the time" on news (NewsGuard's AI page). To brands it sells Brand Misinformation Monitoring, a real-time service "to identify and respond to emerging false narratives before they cause reputational harm", tracking false narratives about a brand across social platforms, GenAI outputs and websites, with early warning alerts and "actionable insights into how clients are represented—or misrepresented—by AI models" (the service's page). The Capture Registry holds the center to the catalogue: False Claim Fingerprints and the Brand Misinformation Monitoring Service "are NewsGuard's commercial products", the composition at the center's name files them under the center as "Core Tools & Resources", and so "the entity widens from a catalogue to a company's offer", while "The record's center holds the content-farm catalogue and the False Claim Monitor series" and "The record keeps the catalogue as the entity" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29). NewsGuard was launched in March 2018 by Steven Brill and Gordon Crovitz and provides credibility ratings and "Nutrition Labels" for news and information websites, licensed by browsers, news aggregators, education companies, and social media and search platforms (the launch release); the MMRS record gives NewsGuard as the center's operator, on the basis of the center's own page (MMRS record). Wikipedia's article on NewsGuard opens "NewsGuard is a rating system for news and information websites", files it in its short description as a "Browser plugin", dates the company's founding to 2018 by Brill and L. Gordon Crovitz, and says the company also provides misinformation tracking and brand safety (Wikipedia, NewsGuard). Its section on disinformation in AI reports that NewsGuard "has audited the output of various AI models to identify disinformation", that leading generative AI tools repeated false news claims 35% of the time on average in August 2025, that Sora 2 produced videos advancing fake claims in 80% of cases, and that, according to NewsGuard, Russian propaganda networks are attempting to "infect" large language models (Wikipedia, NewsGuard); it has no section on the center, and a search of English Wikipedia's articles for the phrase AI Tracking Center answers "There were no results matching the query." (Wikipedia, 2026-10-29). At the center's name on Google's AI Overview on 29 October 2026 the Capture Registry reads a composition that "gives what the center tracks, its headline figures, and the NewsGuard tools around it, all from NewsGuard's pages", with "3,749 sites in 16 languages" the record's figure, checked that day against the MMRS record and the entity's own pages, and states that "The video-recognition failure rates and the 67% blocking figure are not verified here" (Capture Registry, 2026-10-29); the MMRS record links that composition as "the composition layer's account of the entity" (MMRS record).
